title: Five Questions with with Meghan Macdonald, Director of Communications
body_markdown:
Meghan Macdonald joined Expand Energy in September as Director of Communications, bringing international energy experience and a focus on helping people understand and connect with our company’s story.


***How do you describe your role to someone outside the communications field?*** After I emceed our recent town hall, Mike \[Chairman Wichterich\] jokingly asked me, “Were you a cruise director?” It made me laugh because that’s actually an analogy I’ve used to explain what I do!


From an employee communications standpoint, I’m trying to get everyone inside the boat dancing to the same song and singing the same tune. That means helping everyone understand where we’re headed, how they fit into the journey and how we can all move in the same direction. I also want people to feel excited about working here. The way we tell our story plays a big role in that.


Externally, I think of our stakeholders as the different ports of call. I help prepare our people for those interactions so they know what to expect, can communicate our story clearly and can build positive relationships that advance our business priorities.


***What drew you to Expand Energy, and what approach are you bringing to the communications function?*** Expand Energy is incredibly well positioned for the future. Its strategy and the way it’s diversifying to capitalize on growing demand for natural gas really appealed to me. After several years working overseas, I was also really excited to work for an American producer.


Most importantly, the people really stood out to me during the interview process. Everyone I met was nice, talented and collaborative. That’s the kind of environment I want to work in. Two months in, the experience has exceeded my expectations.


As far as my role goes, I want to make sure communications adds strategic value to the business and helps our company capture the opportunities ahead. I feel well positioned to do that at Expand Energy because communications has a seat at the table, insight into what’s happening and colleagues who are eager to engage.


I also love the company’s commitment to continuous improvement, which our new CEO Danny \[Brown\] really embodies. No matter how well things are working today, there’s always an opportunity to make them better, and that’s the mindset I bring to communications.


***What excites you most about Expand Energy’s future?*** There’s almost too much to list! We’ve just welcomed Danny as our new CEO, and we have an incredible leadership team and a strong strategy to capture the opportunities ahead for natural gas.


It feels like a trifecta: the right people, the right strategy and the right market conditions. This is exactly where I want to be working in energy right now.


***What drew you to the energy sector, and what has kept you here?*** A former boss and mentor once explained it to me this way: you can’t do anything without energy. It’s fundamental to everything that happens in the world. People get excited about AI, technology and other industries, but none of those can exist without energy.


What’s kept me here is seeing the human impact. I’ve been fortunate to spend time in places where access to affordable, reliable energy looks very different from what we’re used to in the United States. Seeing how that access can transform people’s lives gives you a real appreciation for this industry. I love being part of something so fundamental to human progress.


***What do you like to do outside of work?*** Spoil my pets! I work hard so they can have a better life. My husband and I have one dog — a rescue mutt — and three formerly stray cats who are now all living a life of luxury.
